ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, $CB = CA$, $CE \perp AB$ at point $E$, point $F$ is a point on $CE$, extend $AF$ to intersect $BC$ at point $D$, $CG \perp AD$ at point $G$, connect $EG$. As shown in Figure 2, if $GC = 2$ and $GE = 2\sqrt{2}$, find the length of $GD$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $CB=CA$, and $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAC=45^\circ$,\\
Since $CE\perp AB$, and $CG\perp AD$,\\
it implies that $\angle AGC=\angle AEC=90^\circ$, and $\angle ACE=45^\circ$,\\
Therefore, points A, C, G, E are concyclic,\\
hence $\angle AGE=\angle ACE=45^\circ$,\\
As shown in Figure 2, draw EH$\perp$AD at point H through point E,\\
thus $\triangle EGH$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$EH=GH=GE\cdot \sin 45^\circ=2\sqrt{2}\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=2$,\\
Since $CG=2$,\\
it follows that $CG=EH$,\\
Since $\angle CGF=\angle EHF=90^\circ$, and $\angle CFG=\angle EFH$,\\
therefore $\triangle CFG\cong \triangle EFH$ (by AAS),\\
thus $FG=FH=1$, and $CF=EF$,\\
In $\triangle CFG$, $CF=\sqrt{CG^2+FG^2}=\sqrt{2^2+1^2}=\sqrt{5}$,\\
thus $CE=2CF=2\sqrt{5}$,\\
thus $AC=\frac{CE}{\sin\angle CAE}=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{\sin 45^\circ}=2\sqrt{10}$,\\
thus $AG=\sqrt{AC^2-CG^2}=\sqrt{(2\sqrt{10})^2-2^2}=6$,\\
Since $\angle CGD=\angle AGC=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle CAG+\angle ACG=90^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle ACG+\angle DCG=90^\circ$,\\
it implies that $\angle CAG=\angle DCG$,\\
Therefore, $\triangle CAG\sim \triangle DCG$,\\
thus $\frac{DG}{CG}=\frac{CG}{AG}$,\\
thus $DG=\frac{CG^2}{AG}=\frac{2^2}{6}=\boxed{\frac{2}{3}}$.

In Figure 2, the base BA of triangle ABC is horizontal, vertex C is above, and CE is drawn from C perpendicular to the base AB and intersects it at E; point F is on CE, while the oblique line AD passes through A and F and extends upward to the left to intersect BC at D; from C a perpendicular is drawn to AD, with foot G, a right angle is marked at G in the figure, and EG is connected. From CE⊥AB and CG⊥AD, we know ∠AEC=90° and ∠AGC=90°, so the four points A, C, G, E are concyclic. Thus angles subtended by the same arc are equal, ∠AGE=∠ACE=45°. Draw EH⊥AD through E, with foot H. Because G and H are on AD, ∠EHG=90°, and ∠EGH=∠AGE=45°, △EGH is a 45°-45°-90° isosceles right triangle. From GE=2√2, we get EH=GH=GE·sin45°=2√2·(√2/2)=2. It is also known that CG=2, so CG=EH. Since CG⊥AD and EH⊥AD, ∠CGF=∠EHF=90°; F is on CE and G, F, H are on AD, so ∠CFG and ∠EFH are equal acute angles formed by CE and AD. Therefore △CFG≅△EFH, giving CF=EF and FG=FH. In Figure 2, F is located between G and H, and GH=2, so FG=FH=1. In right triangle △CFG, CF=√(CG²+FG²)=√(2²+1²)=√5. Because CF=EF, CE=CF+EF=2√5. △ACE is a 45°-45°-90° right triangle, so AC=CE/sin45°=2√5/(√2/2)=2√10. In right triangle △ACG, AG=√(AC²-CG²)=√((2√10)²-2²)=√(40-4)=6. Finally, because D is on BC and CG⊥AD, ∠CGD=90°. In right triangle △ACG, ∠CAG+∠ACG=90°; also because CB and CD are the same straight line and ∠ACB=90°, ∠ACG+∠DCG=90°, hence ∠CAG=∠DCG. Thus △CAG∼△DCG, and the corresponding sides satisfy DG/CG=CG/AG. Substituting CG=2 and AG=6, we get DG=CG²/AG=4/6=2/3.
